Margaret Pace Park: Eight bayfront acres in Edgewater with a 27-feature calisthenics rig — the most complete free outdoor training setup in the urban core.
8-acre, high-energy waterfront park in Edgewater just north of Downtown Miami, with an urban Biscayne Bay setting and views toward the Venetian Islands and Miami Beach.

Amenities include basketball, tennis, and sand-volleyball courts, outdoor workout equipment, open grass, bayfront walking paths, shaded playground, picnic tables and BBQ facilities, restrooms, and an enclosed dog park; dogs are allowed on leash elsewhere in the park. Long-term upgrades are planned, so exact facilities may evolve.
Best fit for a social, urban workout or spontaneous game with friends; expect a lively Edgewater community hub rather than a secluded nature-first escape.
On Biscayne Bay in Edgewater — short walk from the Adrienne Arsht Metromover station; street parking on N Bayshore Dr.
Water, sun protection, workout shoes, dog leash if bringing a dog, and basketball/volleyball/tennis gear if playing.
After work for the social workout scene, pickup games, runners, dog owners, basketball players, and volleyball groups.
The Underline — Brickell Backyard: A free outdoor gym under the Metrorail — the first stretch of a 10-mile linear park. Proof that Miami's best training real estate costs nothing.
Bodyweight circuit at the Urban Gym (sponsored by Baptist Health), then a run north on the trail toward the Miami River. Free group fitness events run regularly — check their calendar.
Directly below Brickell Metrorail station — take the train. The trail itself is the running route.
Venetian Pool: A 1920s quarry turned spring-fed swimming grotto — caves, waterfalls, and the most beautiful public pool in America. Not a lap pool; a ritual.
Go on a weekday at opening (11am) before the families arrive — swim the grotto, then sit under the waterfall. Kids must be 3+ and 38 inches tall.
In the Gables residential core near the Biltmore — free lot parking on site.
Flamingo Park: Flamingo Park is the rare South Beach spot where you can stack a swim, track workout, tennis hit, playground visit, or dog walk in one central community hub.
Think of Flamingo Park as South Beach’s recreation campus: lap pool, water playground, 17 tennis courts, track, fields, basketball, handball/racquetball, playgrounds, walking paths, and dog park.
Inside Flamingo Park, SoBe's big recreation block — street parking around Jefferson/Michigan or the 12th St garages.
Early morning for lap swim / track; late afternoon for tennis, playground, and park time.
Pulse Fitness: Reformer-based training right on Sunset Drive — the South Miami answer to the boutique pilates wave that's mostly stayed north of the Gables.

Boutique, Pilates-inspired reformer studio in South Miami offering 50-minute, low-impact but high-intensity classes that blend strength training, endurance work, and controlled Pilates-style movement.
Classes are booked in advance. Private classes may be available by arrangement.

Small-group resistance-based reformer sessions are designed to challenge core strength, stability, muscular endurance, and tone. South Miami classes cap around 12 people, so the feel should be more coached and personal than a large gym class. Offerings include full-body reformer, arms-and-abs, Pilates, high-intensity Pilates, Lagree-style formats, and private classes by arrangement.
A strong cross-training option if you want strength and muscular endurance work that is easier on joints than running or traditional HIIT.
On Sunset Drive in downtown South Miami — metered street parking and city garages; walkable from South Miami Metrorail.
Grip socks, water, and comfortable fitted workout clothes for reformer work.
Book ahead; schedule runs early morning through evening but varies by day and class format.
Matheson Hammock Park: The man-made atoll pool flushed by the tide is one of Miami's genuinely unique swims — salt water, skyline views, and mangroves on Old Cutler.
Swim the atoll pool at high tide when it's freshest, then rent a kayak or SUP from the PADL self-service kiosk and paddle the mangrove channels.
Off Old Cutler Rd between the Gables and Pinecrest — on the Old Cutler bike trail. Parking $5 weekdays, $7 weekends/holidays.
Polestar Pilates Studio — Dadeland: The flagship studio of a global pilates education company — where the people who train the trainers actually teach. The rehab-and-precision end of the spectrum.
If you're working around an injury, book a private first — rehabilitation is Polestar's actual specialty, not a marketing line.
In the Dadeland area — lot parking; near Dadeland North Metrorail.
Crandon Park: 808 acres with a two-mile Atlantic beach, running trails, and the tennis center that used to host the Miami Open. A full training day disguised as a beach trip.
Early-morning beach run on the hard-packed sand at low tide — two miles out, two back, then swim. Parking fee applies but entry is free.
On Key Biscayne via the Rickenbacker — combine with the causeway ride/run. Parking lots at the beach (fee).
Reserve Padel — Design District: The members-only sibling — three glass courts dropped into the middle of the Design District's fashion blocks. Padel as a luxury good.
This location is members-only — if you're not ready to commit, play the Seaplane Base first and decide whether the Reserve ecosystem is your scene.
NE 39th St in the Design District core. District garages within a block.
Ultra Padel Club (Magic City): 29 courts — the largest padel facility in the US, with a pool and wellness center attached. The volume play: always a court, always a game.
Book an outdoor court (from $28/90min) via Playtomic, or jump into a group clinic ($60/90min) if you need a game — open matchmaking is the fastest way in.
In the Magic City Innovation District, Little Haiti — on-site parking. 10 minutes from Wynwood or the Design District.
Ahana Yoga: The Design District's home studio — power vinyasa to restorative, with breath and present-moment awareness built into everything they run.
Design District yoga studio built around movement, breath, and community; studio-tested apparel / retail is also part of the brand experience.
Book a class online; choose class type based on desired intensity.

Classes include Ahana Flow, Power Flow, Ashtanga, Mysore, Flow & Restore, and Gentle Yoga. The studio positions itself around breath-led vinyasa, restorative practice, and a Design District community feel.
New students can use the 1-month unlimited intro offer; start with Ahana Flow for the core community experience or Gentle Yoga if you want a softer entry.
In the Miami Design District at 43 NE 38th St — use Design District garages or rideshare during peak shopping / dining hours.
Yoga mat, water, towel, and comfortable practice clothes.
Start with a flow class when you want energy; choose restorative / gentle classes for a reset.
Wynwood Padel Club: The OG — running since 2016, before Miami's padel boom had a name. Beginner-friendly pricing and the least pretentious courts in town.
This is the place to learn — beginner clinics and student memberships from $10 make it the lowest-stakes entry into padel in Miami.
In Wynwood — street and lot parking nearby.
Anatomy Midtown: Miami's flagship luxury gym — where serious lifters and the see-and-be-seen crowd coexist. The equipment and coaching justify the price; the scene is the bonus or the tax, depending on your mood.
Luxury training and recovery club with gym floor, group fitness, locker rooms, steam / sauna / plunges, and recovery tools.
Tour, join, or ask about day-pass access; book classes / services ahead when needed.

Amenities include group fitness, state-of-the-art equipment, eucalyptus steam room, hot and cold plunges, infrared and traditional sauna, locker rooms, complimentary parking, Normatec compression boots, Theraguns, Dyson hairdryers, and Malin + Goetz products.
Use Midtown when you want the classic Anatomy mix: serious equipment, group fitness, steam, sauna, hot/cold plunges, and recovery tools in one polished club.
NE 2nd Ave in Midtown. Garage parking at Midtown Miami retail garages a block away.
The Standard Spa: Miami's original wellness-as-lifestyle property. Hamam, arctic plunge, and a bayfront infinity pool where the pace slows down on its own.
Book a spa service over $125 on a Mon–Thu — it unlocks the full hydrotherapy playground (hamam, plunge, sauna, steam, infinity pool).
On Belle Isle, first island on the Venetian Causeway from the Beach side. Valet at the hotel; bike over the Venetian for the best arrival.
Carillon Miami Wellness Resort: The largest spa on the Eastern Seaboard — 70,000 sq ft of thermal circuit, including Miami's only Arctic igloo. This is the deep end of recovery.

Large beachfront wellness resort with 70,000 square feet of spa and wellness space, thermal / hydrotherapy-style amenities, touchless wellness technology, ocean-view fitness center, spa, beach club, pools, and fresh / organic dining.
Book a day experience, spa service, retreat, or hotel stay in advance; confirm which amenities are included with your booking.

Carillon positions itself as an integrative wellness resort with Western, Eastern, alternative, and aesthetic medicine; offerings include spa treatments, touchless wellness therapies, IV therapy, chakra balancing, salt bath therapy, fitness center access, and 65+ fitness classes per week.
Book a day experience or spa treatment when you want the full 70,000-square-foot wellness ecosystem: thermal circuit, touchless wellness, ocean-view fitness, and beach-club energy.
Beachfront on Collins Ave at 68th in North Beach. Valet / hotel parking is the simplest option; street parking on Collins can be limited.
Swimsuit, sandals, workout clothes, water bottle, and a change of clothes; bring ID and payment card for spa / beach club check-in.
Weekdays for a quieter spa day; morning if pairing fitness classes with thermal recovery.
Reserve Padel — Seaplane Base: Padel with seaplanes landing behind you — five glass courts on the water, a beachfront deck, and a bar. The most cinematic racquet venue in Miami.
Book a non-member court at an off-peak weekday slot — you don't need a membership to play, and daytime rates run meaningfully below peak evening/weekend pricing.
Watson Island, on the MacArthur Causeway between Downtown and South Beach. On-site parking; 10 minutes from Brickell or SoBe.
BÜNDA Coral Gables: Boxing, Muay Thai, and Jiu-Jitsu on Merrick Way — glute-focused branding, genuinely tough programming.
Coral Gables studio with showers, bathrooms, changing rooms, and Hyperice recovery tools; the workout centers on BÜNDA’s glute-focused strength / conditioning format.
Book a class online, arrive early for orientation, and validate parking if using the Baptist Hospital structure on Giralda Ave.

New-client offer listed as one week unlimited for $39. Amenities include parking validation, showers, bathrooms, changing rooms, and recovery tools. Do not park at Denny’s or Legacy Fit across the street; towing warning is explicit on the studio page.
Book the signature BÜNDA class and arrive 10 minutes early for the equipment rundown — it's glute-focused strength with nightclub energy, and the room moves fast.

Merrick Way just off Miracle Mile. $1 validated parking (75 min) at the Baptist Hospital parking structure — entrance on Giralda Ave. Do NOT park at Denny's or Legacy Fit across the street (tow risk); metered street parking also available.
Training shoes, water, towel, and clothes for strength / cardio work; arrive early for first-class setup.
Before or after work for high-energy class atmosphere; book ahead for peak slots.
Skanda Yoga Studio: Power Vinyasa with an alignment obsession — Brickell's most serious mat practice.
Take the signature Skanda flow and check their new-student intro pricing before buying single classes.
SW 1st Ave at the south edge of Brickell — street parking, or Metrorail/Metromover to Brickell and a 10-minute walk.
Studio Three: 9,000 square feet, three modalities, one very good sound system — Gensler-designed and it shows.
Start with the Interval class — the signature format — then sample Cycle or Yoga on the same roster once you know the room.
NW 29th St in Wynwood — lot parking nearby; rideshare on weekend evenings.
TREMBLE Brickell: Same reformer-cardio hybrid as the Beach location, tucked into the 1060 building mezzanine.
Book the signature reformer-strength class and arrive 15 early for the machine intro — the pace doesn't wait for orientation.
1060 Brickell Ave — garage in the building, or Metromover to Tenth Street/Promenade.
Life Time Gables: Full-service athletic club on South Dixie — also the Wednesday-night starting line for Gables Run Club.
Take the tour before joining — the pool deck, recovery amenities, and class breadth are what justify the price, and promos move month to month.
S Dixie Hwy across from UM — on-site garage; Metrorail University station is directly across the highway.
Fight Sports Club Miami: Roberto 'Cyborg' Abreu's world-champion technique made beginner-friendly — community over intimidation.
Book a fundamentals striking or BJJ class — they onboard true beginners, and the first session tells you if the culture fits.
NE 61st St in Little River — lot and street parking.
Mimi Yoga & Pilates (Wynwood): The original — an instant hit for a design that photographs as well as it stretches you.
Start with a mat class, move to reformer after a couple of visits — the progression is the point here.
NW 27th St — Wynwood lot parking; walkable from the Wynwood core.
The Ice Room: Membership-model cold plunge on Brickell Bay Drive — for people who've made recovery a lifestyle line item.
Book the sauna + plunge contrast circuit — staff walk first-timers through timing and breathing protocols.
Brickell Bay Drive — building garage or metered street; short walk from Brickell City Centre.
Break Free Movement: Hot yoga, mat sculpt, and aerial fitness under one roof — a full cross-training menu in Coral Gables.
Boutique Coral Gables fitness studio focused on heated yoga, mat pilates sculpt, fitness, and strength training.
Book via the Break Free Movement app; also on ClassPass and Wellhub (Titanium plan tier).

Break Free Movement describes itself as a “hot spot” in Coral Gables serving Miami, Coconut Grove, South Miami, and Brickell. The programming blends heated yoga, mat pilates sculpt, fitness, and strength rather than a single-modality yoga room.
Start with their mobility-meets-strength fusion class — it's the clearest expression of what the studio does differently.
Ponce de Leon Blvd near UM — parking in the building; metered street as backup.
Yoga mat, towel, water, grip socks if needed for pilates-style formats, and clothes for a heated class.
After work for a lively heated class; weekend morning if pairing with Gables errands.
Suva Yoga: Sound bowls and slow flows on Alhambra Circle — the antidote to a Brickell trading day.
Book a slow flow first — it's a small, quiet Gables room and the gentler classes show it at its best.
Alhambra Circle — metered street parking around the Gables business district.
Mimi Yoga & Pilates (Coconut Grove): Infrared-heated flows in a design-forward space — Mimi's second location after Wynwood proved the concept.
Same play as the Wynwood original: mat class first, reformer once you know the style.
Bird Ave in the Grove — street parking or the CocoWalk garages a few blocks over.
Om Movement: Yoga, Pilates, and kettlebells a quarter-mile from Peacock Park, plus a free community class every first Friday.
Book an evening flow — second-floor space above the Grove's main drag, and the after-work classes carry the community.
McFarlane Rd in the Grove center — CocoWalk or Oak Ave garages; easy walk from anywhere in the village.
JETSET Pilates Sunset Harbour: 50 minutes of reformer-meets-cardio in the heart of Sunset Harbour's fitness strip.
Book the 50-minute signature reformer class and arrive 15 early — it's fast-paced and beginner spots go quickly at peak times.
Sunset Harbour — 1900 Bay Rd garage is the reliable move.
Centner Wellness Gables: Centner Gables is the recovery-first longevity hub—less flagship polish, more stress reset, regulation, and recharge.
Recovery-first Centner location on Coral Way focused on stress relief, nervous-system support, recovery, energy, and holistic biohacking.
Bookings managed through the Centner Wellness mobile app.

Best positioned as the Centner option for regulation and recharge rather than a gym. Good shareable angle: book for recovery, stress reset, and premium wellness treatments; verify current service menu by location.
Best Centner pick for a nervous-system reset: stress relief, recovery, energy, and holistic biohacking.
Coral Way at the Gables edge — lot parking at the unit.
Comfortable clothes; follow appointment-specific prep instructions.
Weekdays or slower appointment windows; book ahead.
Pause Studio Brickell: Private infrared sauna, cold plunge, and float therapy — contrast therapy without the locker-room energy.
The sauna + cold plunge circuit is the entry point; add a float once you've done contrast a couple of times.
SW 9th St — garage in the building; two blocks from Brickell City Centre.
Casa Vinyasa: Infrared-heated, home-like, and built by a teacher who wanted the Gables to have real community yoga.
Infrared-heated Coral Gables yoga studio designed to feel home-like and community-oriented, with heated power flows, active recovery, mat pilates, and more.
Buy the new-student special or book a class online; arrive early if it’s your first heated class.

All instructors are 200-hour Registered Yoga Instructors. Classes are designed to support and challenge, with options from heated power flows to active recovery and mat pilates. Founder Melissa Echevarria opened Casa Vinyasa in 2017 after teaching across Miami since 2014.
Classic vinyasa — check the new-student intro pricing before buying single classes.
S Dixie Hwy near UM — plaza lot parking at the door.
Yoga mat, towel, water, and clothes for a heated studio.
Heated flow when you want work; active recovery or mat pilates when you want something gentler / cross-training oriented.
LEGACY Little River: 12,000-square-foot flagship built around partner interval training — HIIT with a community backbone.
Book a coached small-group session — this is a training gym with programming, not a machines-and-headphones gym.
NW Miami Ct in Little River — lot parking on site.
Wynwood Yoga Studio: Hot power yoga, Mysore mornings, candlelit Yin at night — a full schedule for every mood.
Check the new-student pass and start with an all-levels flow — the community feel is the draw here.
NW 5th Ave — Wynwood lot and street parking.
Open Door Yoga: Playful, all-levels, and unpretentious — flow, Yin, and something called 'Funyasa.'
Book ahead — it's a small Grove room — and start with the slower flow before the stronger classes.
Florida Ave — Grove street parking; walkable from the village center.
TREMBLE Miami Beach: Low-impact, high-intensity reformer work that leaves you shaking — literally the point.
Book the signature reformer-strength class, arrive 15 early for the machine intro — same drill as the Brickell location.
West Ave — 1900 Bay Rd garage nearby; bikeable from most of South Beach.
Raw Fit-Miami: Circuit and functional training near Little Haiti Soccer Park — no frills, just work.
Book a fundamentals group session first — the coached classes are the core of the gym, not an add-on.
NE 4th Ave — lot and street parking in Little River.
SWEAT440 Brickell: 40-minute strength classes starting every 10 minutes — no excuse not to fit it in.
Classes start every 10 minutes, so just show up — and check their standing free-first-class intro offer before paying.
SW 9th St — building garage; two blocks off Brickell Ave.
Pause Studio Coral Gables: Same private suite model as Brickell, plus a $35 'Sauna Social' if you want company in the heat.
Sauna + cold plunge circuit first visit, float later — same playbook as their Brickell studio.
Plaza Coral Gables on Palermo — garage in the complex.
